headline: Monday snapped a 7-day slide: S&P 500 +4.7%, Nasdaq +6.5%, Dow +3.0% as Nvidia jumped about 31% after Huang was reinstated as CEO. Oil fell to a 3-month low. A Dec 9 Fed hike is still expected; VIX about 27. PCE due Wednesday, market shut Thursday.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. A December 9 Fed hike is still widely expected and the flash services PMI cooled to 54.7, a mild headwind but not a clear direction.
No specific US telecom news. Communication services rose about 3.6% in Monday's rebound, but long Treasury yields near 5.3% weigh on dividend payers.
A December 9 Fed hike is still widely expected and the 10-year yield held near 4.92%, keeping mortgage and auto loan costs high for homes, cars and furniture.
Staples were flat (about -0.1%) on Monday as money rotated back into tech after being last week's hiding place. Lower oil eases costs slightly. J.M. Smucker reports today.
Lower oil (WTI near $80, lowest close since late August) helps travel and leisure costs, but rate-hike expectations and a cooling PMI limit the upside.
No clear sector news. The flash composite PMI fell to 54.6, its lowest since July, which hints at slower demand but is still expansion.

Chips led Monday's bounce (tech about +9%, Nvidia about +31% after Huang was reinstated as CEO, upgrades for Nvidia and Texas Instruments), but it follows a roughly 39% one-month Nvidia drop, open Nvidia investigations and a VIX still near 27. Dell and HP report after today's close.

Oil slid again Monday: Brent about -3.5% to near $89 and WTI about -3.9% to near $80, its lowest close since late August, on Libya restarting the Sharara pipeline, higher Middle East exports and surplus forecasts. Energy was the worst sector Monday.
Financials rose about 2% Monday. A flat yield curve (2-year 4.63%, 10-year 4.92%) and an expected December hike give no clear one-month direction.
No clear sector news since the close. Health care lagged Monday's rally (about +1.2%).
No clear sector news. Medtronic reports before today's open; Agilent rose about 8% after hours on a beat and strong guidance.
Industrials rose about 3.9% Monday, but the PMI cooled and there is no sector-specific news pointing one way for a month.
No clear news for this group.
Materials rose about 3.2% Monday with the broad market, but there is no clear metals news to point one way for a month.
Cheaper oil lowers input costs for chemicals makers, but slower PMI demand offsets it. No clear direction.
Flash manufacturing PMI at 54.5 is still expansion but the composite is at its lowest since July; Deere reports Wednesday. No clear direction.
Lower gasoline costs help shoppers before the holiday season, but rates stay high. Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Burlington, Dick's, Abercrombie and Kohl's report before today's open, so wait for results.

CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion and raised guidance, but CRWD fell about 9%; Oracle said its OpenAI contract funding is secured. Workday and Autodesk report after today's close.
Oil fell to its lowest close since late August (WTI near $80), which cuts fuel costs for airlines, truckers and railroads if it lasts.
Utilities rose about 1.5% Monday but long yields near 5.3% and an expected December hike weigh on them, while AI power demand supports them. No clear direction.

avoid.NVDA: Huge 31% one-day rebound after CEO turmoil, with open investigations including an accounting review reported; news-driven swings make a month-long hold risky.
